rationale: links.webdesign.uk is a public hostname whose nginx proxies customer clicks into the cluster, to core-manager:8088 — the same port that serves the whole admin API (every site's data, the work-item queue, the pipeline controls, the agent-definition writes). The only thing between the internet and that API is an anchored `location` regex in a config file on a box: widen it to `/` and the admin API is public, and nothing in the binary would notice or refuse. This change moves the customer delivery routes (/c/, later /d/) onto a SECOND HTTP listener in core-manager and repoints the box vhost and the WireGuard egress fence at it, so that widening that location can expose the delivery routes and nothing else. The owner ruled BUILD on 2026-08-25 (RFC_054 §5 Q2), asking for a plan and a council round of its own; the plan is at site_delivery_and_editor/PLAN_2026-08-25_delivery_only_listener.md. The routes are MOVED, not copied — a copy leaves the hole open — and the invariant is enforced at construction rather than by review, because this tree has repeatedly failed to hold properties held only by review. I am flagging three things for the seats rather than waiting to be asked: (1) the containment is partial and I have not hidden that — port 8088 stays on the egress fence because the chat bot's facts relay needs it, so a NEW vhost written straight to :8088 would still reach the admin API; closing that means moving the facts relay too, which touches a live customer-facing bot and is outside the ruling's scope. (2) assertNoDeliveryRoutes fails CLOSED, refusing to construct the server; the alternative is log-and-continue, which nobody reads, but crash-looping core-manager is a real cost and I would take an overrule on it. (3) There is a window between the core-manager roll and the box repoint in which /c/ returns 404 at the box; customer_access_tokens = 0 and no delivery email has ever been sent, so the measured impact is zero, and the box file carries a DO-NOT-APPLY-BEFORE-THE-ROLL header rather than relying on whoever applies it remembering.
submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane, executing RFC_054 Q2 (owner ruling 2026-08-25). Joint lane with webdesign_uk_build_service, whose box vhost this repoints.

plan.summary: core-manager gains a second http.Server whose gin.Engine registers ONLY the delivery routes, via the handler's existing RegisterRoutes (the single route-table definition, so there is no second copy to drift). The delivery routes are removed from the main router. The listener is opt-in through a new config key server.delivery_port with the unsafe default OFF: unset means no listener AND the customer routes mounted nowhere, never a fallback onto the admin port. Production opts in in the overlay, where a reviewer of the deployment sees the decision. assertNoDeliveryRoutes walks the main router's real route table at construction and returns an error — refusing to build the server — if any /c/ or /d/ path is mounted there. The wg egress fence adds core-manager:8090 (keeping 8088 for the chat bot's facts relay) and the box vhost proxies to :8090. platform/config gains an explicit BindEnv for the new key because viper's AutomaticEnv cannot reach a key absent from both the config file and the defaults: without it the overlay reads perfectly and the listener never starts.

edits.rationale: The load-bearing half. The delivery routes are MOVED off the admin router, not copied onto a second one: a copy would leave the admin port publicly reachable and buy nothing. The removed block is replaced by a comment that states where they went and why, because a reader of this function otherwise has no way to discover that the routes exist at all.
edits.sketch:
// BEFORE — in setupRoutes, mounted on the ADMIN router:
-	deliveryHandler := handlers.NewDeliveryHandler(
-		handlers.NewDBDeliveryDeps(personaRepoImpl.ClientsDB(), s.logger))
-	deliveryHandler.RegisterRoutes(s.router)

// AFTER — the routes are gone from this router entirely; the block above is
// replaced by the comment below, and the handler is constructed in NewServer
// against the DELIVERY engine instead (see the newDeliveryServer edit).
+	// THE CUSTOMER DELIVERY ROUTES (/c/, later /d/) ARE DELIBERATELY NOT HERE.
+	// They live on a SECOND listener with its own router (newDeliveryEngine),
+	// so that this port — which serves every site's data, the work-item queue
+	// and the pipeline controls — carries no publicly-reachable customer route
+	// at all. Before 2026-08-25 they were mounted here, and the only thing
+	// keeping the admin API off the internet was an anchored `location` regex
+	// in nginx on the webdesign.uk box. RFC_054 Q2, owner ruling 2026-08-25.
+	// Enforced, not intended: assertNoDeliveryRoutes refuses to construct the
+	// server if a delivery path is ever mounted on this router.

edits.rationale: The property this change buys is 'the admin port serves no customer route'. Held only by review, that lasts until the first session that adds a route back for a good local reason and leaves the suite green. Checked against the REAL route table at construction, it becomes something the process refuses to start without. Fail-closed is deliberate and is the item I most want the seats to challenge: the only way to trip it is to mount a customer route on the admin port, which is exactly the mistake it exists to catch, but the cost of a false positive is a crash-looping core-manager.

newDeliveryEngine registers the delivery routes and nothing else — no health endpoint, no metrics, no catch-all — because 'delivery-only' is the whole value and anything mounted here is reachable from the internet. Routes come from the handler's own RegisterRoutes, which is the single definition of the route table (the guardian seat's mirror-drift objection on council ea99befa), so there is no second copy here to drift. newDeliveryServer is a separate function rather than an inline if, specifically so the default-OFF direction can be asserted by a test: the safety of the whole mechanism rests on which way the empty case falls.

StartDelivery returns nil immediately when unconfigured so main.go need not mirror the opt-in decision. Shutdown closes the public door FIRST and deliberately does not let its error mask the main one — a customer mid-click is a smaller loss than an admin request killed with the error swallowed.

THE DEFECT THIS BUILD ALREADY CAUGHT, recorded rather than smoothed over. server.delivery_port is set only by core-manager's production overlay and named in no service's YAML. viper's Unmarshal populates from viper's known key set, and AutomaticEnv alone does not add a key absent from both the config file and the defaults — so without an explicit BindEnv the env var is silently ignored, the listener never starts, and every customer link 404s at the box with the overlay reading perfectly correct and no error anywhere in the cluster. I wrote the test before the bind and it FAILED, which is the only reason this is a paragraph rather than a live outage. Binding affects no other service: unset stays empty, which is the OFF default.

Each of the three properties is asserted rather than described. The route-table test asserts an EXACT count, not a sample of paths that happen to 404 — a sample cannot fail when someone adds a route. TestDeliveryEngineReachesTheHandler is the control for the 404 sweep: without it, a delivery engine that served nothing at all (a typo'd route) would pass every 404 assertion and look like perfect containment.

Adds :8090 so the box can reach the delivery listener; the fence is deny-by-default, so without this the vhost times out in a way that reads as core-manager being down. 8088 STAYS, and the comment says why in the file rather than in a doc: the chat bot's facts relay needs it, so this fence is NOT the containment and must not be read as one. That is the residual I am asking the seats to look at hardest.
edits.sketch:
- to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: core-manager
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8088
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8090

edits.rationale: The opt-in itself, placed in the overlay rather than configs/core-manager.yaml on purpose: this is the one line that makes a port publicly reachable, so the decision belongs where a reviewer of the DEPLOYMENT sees it (CLAUDE.md 2026-08-02 §2). base/service.yaml and base/deployment.yaml declare the port; the env var is what makes it listen.

# Unset it and the delivery routes are served NOWHERE: core-manager
            # will not fall back to mounting them on 8088, which is the whole

            #

grounded_in: OWNER RULING 2026-08-25, RFC_054 §5 Q2, verbatim: "Q2 — BUILD the delivery-only listener. Its own plan + council round; aim to land it before the first customer_access_tokens row exists. It does NOT gate the shopfront unparking, which no longer touches core-manager at all (/c/ moved to links.webdesign.uk, 2026-08-24). Until the listener lands, the box nginx location regex is the stated — not hidden — last line."

RFC_054 §2 Q2's own statement of the problem: "Today the links door proxies to core-manager:8088 — the SAME port that serves the whole admin API. The defence is the nginx location regex, i.e. configuration on a box. ... The trade to rule on: is box-nginx config an acceptable last line, or must the blast radius be capped in the binary?"

COUNTERS RE-MEASURED BY ME, 2026-08-25, not carried forward: `SELECT count(*) AS sites, count(handed_over_at), count(transfer_confirmed_at), count(live_link_expires_at) FROM sites;` returned 51 | 0 | 0 | 0, and `SELECT count(*) FROM customer_access_tokens;` returned 0. This is what makes the roll-to-repoint window zero-impact: no customer can be holding a link.

DEPLOY STATE MEASURED BY ME, 2026-08-25, with the reversed control: the running core-manager stamps `git_commit 4c996e1b5cb9b2513d88ec9fe2bae220c38fb6c2` (build provenance, 09:26Z). `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says fa3b665ed (Phase 4 state) and 882622629 (presign clamp) ARE ancestors — control passes — while 24b63120d and d1a4bdcdf (the second-click split, committed 12:34/12:40Z) are NOT. So this change lands on the same roll as the second-click page.

THE ENV-BINDING DEFECT, PROVEN BEFORE IT WAS FIXED: I wrote TestDeliveryPortIsReadFromTheEnvironment against the unmodified loader and it FAILED with `Server.DeliveryPort = "", want "8090"`. That is the disconfirming result; the test passes only after the explicit BindEnv. Without it the overlay would have read perfectly and the listener would never have started. Recorded because the failure mode is invisible at every other layer.

MUTATION RESULTS, RUN BY ME 2026-08-25 (each mutation applied, suite run, file restored; clean suite green afterwards at -count=1): (1) assertNoDeliveryRoutes returning nil early -> 2 tests FAIL; (2) empty port defaulting ON -> TestDeliveryListenerIsOptInAndDefaultsOff FAILS; (3) an extra route on the delivery engine -> 2 tests FAIL; (4) delivery engine registering nothing -> 2 tests FAIL including the reach control.

CONSUMER CENSUS RUN BY ME 2026-08-25 (RFC_022's 'enumerate the consumers' condition; asserting it without the query is itself the objection): the only consumer of the /c/ route outside this package is `box/links.webdesign.uk.nginx` — `grep -rln 'location.*"\^/c/\|/c/<token>\|/c/:token'` over the box dirs, internal/ and platform/ returns exactly that vhost plus delivery.go, delivery_test.go and my new test. Every other reference to core-manager:8088 in the repo (auth-service configmap, configmap-common, terraform, docker-compose, dev configs) is an INTERNAL service URL for the admin API, which keeps serving everything it served except /c/.

THE RESIDUAL, from the egress fence's own comment which I did not weaken: "core-manager:8088 — box nginx `location /c/` AND the chat bot's facts relay (/api/v1/site-facts/:domain, box/chat-service/facts.go). Breaking this stops the bot STARTING, by its own design." This is why 8088 stays on the allowlist and why I claim only that the EXISTING customer door cannot be widened into the admin API — not that the fence contains it.

VERIFICATION PLANNED FROM OUTSIDE, because inside proves nothing here — LANDMINES.md, footprint links.webdesign.uk.nginx: "anything with a suffix, a prefix segment or a differently-shaped token never crosses WireGuard at all. The box answers 404 locally. Your handler is never reached, so there is no log line, no metric and no error anywhere in the cluster; go test passes, gin's route dump looks right, and a curl from inside the cluster (or against the pod) works perfectly. The failure exists only on the path a real customer takes, and only from outside." The containment check is `curl core-manager:8090/api/v1/admin/work-items` -> 404 PAIRED with the same path against :8088 -> not-404, because the 404 alone would pass against a typo'd hostname.

BUILD PROOF, RUN BY ME 2026-08-25: `scripts/verify-head-builds.sh --test --with <5 changed Go files> ./internal/core-manager/... ./platform/config/... ./cmd/core-manager/...` -> "OK — tests pass against HEAD 58c14d4da". The working tree carries other sessions' WIP, so a local build would not have established this.
